approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a population of molecules with real observed scores. It draws breeding parents from high-scoring quantiles, makes graph crossovers and short random mutation chains, admits valid distinct products, and keeps the best 64 scored survivors. Before each batch it fits a Gaussian process to all accepted observations using raw count fingerprints. It draws correlated functions on the fresh proposal pool and buys distinct maxima, restricting availability to the forty highest predicted means after three non-improving batches. The generator itself never follows a sampled function beyond that completed pool.
approach.novelty: Use one persistent posterior function per requested purchase to guide a bounded graph search from the fresh pool. Each function keeps the same value at a repeated molecule or fingerprint, directs a four-molecule beam through eight mutation waves, and supplies its final distinct maximizer for real evaluation. This adds coherent sampled-function optimization to the Parent. Siblings changed predictive scoring, pool eligibility, local posteriors or persistent observed-return tree counters; the cited earlier continuation chose between two mutations by posterior mean. Here the real predictor and scored population remain the source of knowledge, while temporary function paths guide both construction and purchase. The new search and consumer, including replacement of the old final gate, form one joint intervention.

observed_bottleneck: The actual Parent n-cf8d309c06de spends its learned posterior only on allocating an already completed random graph pool: no latent function value is reused to direct successive construction. Its complete Search panel has 435 full 160-member pools, no posterior fallback, 4350 optimizer purchases and only 634 purchases beating their scored generating roots; the late half has 238/2175. The equal-session positive raw generating-root gain per purchase is 0.0038830439945360625 overall and 0.0020240780825076187 late, while chronological GP MSE rises from 0.009706489512184634 early to 0.013492413138599203 late. These are descriptive limits of the realized stream, not proof that more inner search helps. The available-seed endpoint mean is 0.607030316211131 with population SD 0.030175277546149237. The read-only audit policy/scratch/r0075-01-improve-L01/parent-evidence-audit.json and its fifteen audit-seed-N-task.json files retain the actual summary.json, run.log, optimizer-log and trajectory inputs with hashes. The indexed correction-removal result n-61cb8ba305fa restores this endpoint and the frozen review establishes exact trajectory reproduction; it supplies no new independent replication. n-87c89dda7e3b executed 8640 two-arm posterior-mean continuation decisions on its different exchange-free host yet lost 0.04808254201485503, so this plan does not repeat mean-only polishing. n-8b078abdc05d shows changed prior-origin supply and a concentrated gain on another host, alongside lower accepted prior-product scores and prediction optimism; it is motivation, not transferred component evidence. n-32146d1e11a9 removed dependence under an all-reference cardinal location and lost 0.01313803591803068 despite preserving marginal variance; its host-specific warning motivates coherent dependence rather than independent fitness redraws. The same-Parent mask control n-c501ea219a1c loses 0.010577201922441012 with the original completed-pool Thompson consumer. That contrary result is retained: dropping the old gate here is necessary to purchase optimized path maxima and is priced only as part of this joint search/consumer replacement.

adoptions.applicability: The current Anchor is recovered exactly when the learned correction is removed. n-87c89dda7e3b already refutes the performance promise of two-arm posterior-mean continuation, while n-8b078abdc05d shows that generation refinement can affect useful prior-origin supply under another host. Coherent paths address a different missing capability: one sampled function can guide successive de novo states without changing its value each time, rather than greedily exploiting a fixed mean or merely ranking an already finished field. n-32146d1e11a9 cautions against discarding posterior dependence.
adoptions.borrowed_element: A persistent posterior function, including correct conditioning on real observations, evaluated at adaptively created molecular graphs.; The same cached path controls inner graph-parent/beam selection and the eventual real purchase; samples are never labels.; Bounded de novo acquisition maximization with explicit preservation of raw-count T_DP and recorded computational cost.

Replacing generation and final allocation is a joint intervention.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the frozen Search Policy review and retain its coherent-path adoption and deviations from policy/scratch/round75-search-policy/literature-adoptions.json. Its actual discovery queries remain in the cited review; this PLAN made no new search queries. The three already cited primary paper/code pages were opened for verification. Adopt persistent latent posterior functions and graph acquisition optimization, locally implemented with exact finite conditional Gaussian operations up to the registered float64 rank/roundoff policy. The detailed cache, spectral solves, bounded workload and tests are this intervention's design; the source papers do not establish its gain. Do not adopt Wilson feature approximations, the molecular demonstration's T_MM/UCB or a fixed-library prior sampler. Internal complete Parent evidence supplies the low realized root-gain bottleneck and all contrary-host boundaries. No new model, package or upstream preparation checkpoint is required.

method_change.previous_method: On code Parent n-cf8d309c06de, randomly finish a fresh molecular offspring pool and then allocate real evaluations with correlated GP samples and a stall-conditioned top-mean mask.
method_change.proposed_method: Retain the real accepted-data GP and base generator, jointly replace proposal refinement and final allocation with bounded coherent posterior-path graph optimization and distinct direct path-maximizer purchase.
method_change.rationale: The Parent has no surrogate-directed construction beyond its completed pool. The negative two-arm mean-only result and host-dependent refinement/correlation evidence motivate a different sampled-function search, not a parameter change to the refuted recipe; gate absence is necessary to the registered consumer and is not independently tested.

hypothesis: Modify the proposal-to-purchase boundary on n-cf8d309c06de: keep its accepted-only raw-count T_DP GP and original fresh base-pool generator, then instantiate one independent latent posterior path for each announced batch member. Jointly sample each path on the unique base-pool fingerprints and extend that same finite Gaussian function only at newly admitted fingerprints using the conditional posterior given all its cached values. Use the path to maintain a top-four graph beam across eight waves of at most eight new canonical identities, with at most 96 raw primitive mutation attempts per wave, then execute the highest-valued still-available visited identity in stable path order. Identity and exact-feature aliases share one latent value within a path. Temporary path values never become observations, fitness labels in the real population, or future-session state. The final stall mask and separate final Thompson redraw are absent because the optimized path directly selects its real purchase. This joint replacement predicts novel path maxima reach real feedback and increase equal-session positive generating-root gain per actual optimizer purchase over the complete Parent; endpoint gain is a separate prediction.

finding_summary.headline: Coherent paths reached real purchases, but generating-root gains and endpoint scores fell
finding_summary.insights: This result rules out missing computational exposure or a failure to deliver the path maxima as explanations for the negative result. The borrowed persistent-function and graph-acquisition-search elements operated in the registered exact finite Gaussian adaptation. It does not test the source papers’ feature approximations, UCB settings or performance claims. Maximizing the sampled function farther produced increasingly optimistic selected values: the mean realized-minus-sampled residual was −0.1504 versus −0.1000 in the Parent, and real-GP prediction MSE rose from 0.01160 to 0.01362 on the purchased cohorts. These are consequences measured on different queried distributions, not proof that the GP conditioning algebra or all of its rankings failed. The molecular evidence also shows substantial exploration: typed scaffolds increased from 1,667 to 2,348 and generic scaffolds from 951 to 1,454. The limitation is the usefulness of the newly reached chemistry. The larger-structure tail grew from 46 to 246 products, nitrogen/oxygen-halogen and peroxide connections became more common, and some upper-score cohorts still concentrated on a few cores. These patterns support a diagnosis of poor transfer from optimized surrogate values and broad structural variation to productive observed edits; they do not establish chemical mediation. A proposal operator that preserves useful functional connectivity, or a different surrogate/ranking model for the newly explored graphs, addresses that limitation in kind. Their benefit remains open. The present evidence settles this fixed search-and-purchase recipe’s directional prediction and its negative joint score result; it cannot separate depth, extra graph work, removal of the final stall gate or posterior dependence, and it does not end the broader approach.
finding_summary.results: All three Search seeds completed: 435 allocations and 4,350 optimizer purchases. The numerical replay passed the registered sampling checks. Graph search raised the sampled maximum on 3,397 of 4,350 paths, delivered 3,584 molecules absent from their starting pools, and bought 2,403 products more than one extension edit deep. Those products received real feedback and entered later learning and breeding. The predicted useful-extension benefit did not follow. Mean positive gain over the actual scored generating roots fell from 0.003883 to 0.003035 per purchase; early gain fell from 0.005742 to 0.004563 and late gain from 0.002024 to 0.001508. Purchases beating their roots fell from 634 to 462. The mean endpoint score fell from 0.607030 to 0.564786, a decrease of 0.042245, with all three seed means lower and 13 of 15 task/seed endpoints lower. The 0.609030 endpoint target was missed, and sitagliptin MPO triggered the protocol’s paired task-regression rule. Thus execution and delivery are established, while the registered useful-extension prediction is refuted.

molecular.headline: Broad ring chemistry with larger frameworks, frequent reactive heteroatom bonds and no specified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: This report describes n-eb15da16dbea against its published code Parent n-cf8d309c06de under the frozen Search panel 0/1/2. context.comparison independently marks Child evaluation complete and Parent pairing complete; all fifteen Child and fifteen Parent task trajectories were present. There are no uncovered tasks, missing trajectory paths or absent paired chemistry comparisons. Each task supplies 870 accepted optimizer molecules, excluding the ten supplied initial molecules per session: 4,350 purchased products per node. These are accepted outputs, not the much larger unpurchased proposal population. The Child contains fused, bridged, linked and partially saturated heterocycles, aromatic ethers and amides, cyclic carbonyl/imino/thione motifs, aliphatic amines and extensive halogen substitution. Digest ring-closure marker rates range from 0.9609 to 0.9954 and aromatic marker rates from 0.9425 to 0.9851; these are fractions of SMILES containing markers, not ring counts or aromatic atom fractions. RDKit finds aromatic atoms in 4,213 products. Ring chemistry and amine chemistry are present; the main deficiencies are the consistency of plausible connectivity, compositional size control and stereochemical definition. Median heavy-atom count is 32 versus Parent 28. Both tails remain: 87 products have at most six heavy atoms versus Parent 98, and 246 have at least fifty versus Parent 46; the maxima are 117 and 96. Nitrogen-halogen, oxygen-halogen and oxygen-oxygen bonds occur in 1,384, 525 and 320 Child products versus 888, 162 and 118 Parent products. These connectivity flags do not constitute a synthesis assay. Seventy-seven Child products have an RDKit-perceived all-aromatic ring of at most four atoms, fewer than Parent 170; this is a geometric review flag, not proof that every flagged graph is impossible. There are 3,175 Child products with unassigned tetrahedral stereocentres and none with an assigned centre. Explicit charges occur in 86 Child products, all in the first task; an assertion that charge is universally absent would be incorrect. The full Child set has 2,348 nonempty typed Murcko scaffolds and 1,454 generic scaffolds versus Parent 1,667 and 951. This is broad structural exploration, although several high-score cohorts concentrate on a few families. All 4,350 accepted products join to purchase and feedback receipts without a membership or score discrepancy. Of these, 3,584 are absent from the corresponding allocation base identity list; this descriptive subset has median heavy-atom count 33, 41 products at most six atoms, 244 at least fifty, and 2,232 typed/1,419 generic scaffolds. This membership does not attribute a chemical effect to a component. All purchases, both size tails, early/late phases and base-absent cohorts are retained in the audits. Similarity uses chirality-aware radius-two 2048-bit Morgan Tanimoto between all pairs with more than six heavy atoms, solely as a descriptor; it is not the evaluated GP count kernel, a reward or an admission rule. Pooled per-task high/low deciles contain 87 products each; per-session audits use 29 each. Cohort deciles use the integer floor of one tenth of their own size. Functional-group SMARTS and all method limits are recorded; the fields named carbonyl and amide use uppercase aliphatic carbon SMARTS and must not be read as exhaustive counts of aromatic lactam carbonyls. Synthetic plausibility judgments below also inspect the actual graphs. The report does not infer an unseen target structure, declare an absent motif universally beneficial, rank nodes, assess activation or claim chemical mediation. Methods, input hashes and receipt provenance: policy/scratch/r0075-01-improve-L01/molecular/evidence-manifest.json. Aggregate descriptors and witnesses: policy/scratch/r0075-01-improve-L01/molecular/descriptor-summary.json. The per-task evidence lists cite each derived audit beside both underlying trajectories. Child copies preserve the exact trusted request-listed bytes. Original request-listed evaluation logs were read only; the audits retain their hashes, line identities and membership excerpts, not copied log substitutes.

per_task.generated_character: The products are mostly medium-sized, highly aromatic ring systems: median 25 heavy atoms, range 1–48, with 22 products at most six heavy atoms. The leading seed-0 molecule has 27 heavy atoms, four perceived rings and three aromatic rings: an alkoxy-substituted fused heteroaromatic framework with a sulfur-containing bridge and pyridyl carboxamide; its amide nitrogen is chlorinated. Other leaders are substituted indole/azaindole-like aromatics bearing an exocyclic enamine, phenyl group, hydrazine or N-halogen substituent. These are not simply ring-poor fragments, but their unusual N-S, N-N and N-halogen connectivity makes synthetic plausibility uneven. Parent median size is also 25, while Child typed/generic scaffold counts are 367/159 versus 186/69. Fragment-excluded pair similarity is 0.180265 versus Parent 0.240286; the 642 base-absent products give 0.169392 and 334/151 scaffolds. The defined structural-alert union rises from 99/435 early products to 291/435 late products; this is an output composition observation. Evidence files (each audit alongside its Child and Parent trajectory): policy/scratch/r0075-01-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0075-01-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0075-01-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0075-01-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-1/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-1/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0075-01-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0075-01-improve-L01/molecular/child/seed-2/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-2/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl.
liabilities: Among 870 products, 323 contain N-halogen bonds, 70 O-halogen bonds and 39 O-O bonds. These groups raise stability and synthetic-handling concerns without establishing measured decomposition.
The leading structures include N-chloro amide, N-halogenated aromatic nitrogen and hydrazine-like bonds; a valid SMILES does not establish a practical synthesis.
Very small late products and a very large peroxide-linked aromatic product show that size excursions can discard or overextend the useful ring framework.
missing_features: Consistent access to compact aromatic amide or enamine architectures without accumulating reactive nitrogen/oxygen decoration is not demonstrated; the near-leading unchlorinated amide is an internal witness that comparable observed scores can coexist with fewer such bonds.

A broader set of high-scoring core connectivities is underrepresented despite broad all-output scaffold exploration. The supplied scores do not identify a specific missing ring, nitrile or target ligand.
Stereochemical definition is absent where stereocentres occur; whether configuration would change this objective is not measured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The first cited fused-ring, N-chloro amide scores 0.4248930472866728 at seed 0 evaluation 228. The related unchlorinated amide with a methoxy group scores 0.4215873828756271 at evaluation 293, so the observations do not require an N-halogen bond for a similar score. The seed-1 enamine/hydrazine leader scores 0.4182215872091703; the seed-2 N-bromo enamine scores 0.4173987547377105. In contrast FCl and the small saturated ether C1COC1 score 0.0. The 48-heavy-atom, peroxide-linked aromatic product scores only 5.543355425209431e-18. This panel favors moderately sized, connected aromatic frameworks over both tiny fragments and an oversized concatenation. The Parent best records retain compact aromatic amide/dicarbonyl motifs; no target pharmacophore can be recovered from these associations alone. The Child pooled highest 87 products occupy 13 generic scaffolds, compared with 159 in all 870 products.

liabilities: N-halogen, O-halogen and O-O bonds occur in 491, 145 and 225 of 870 products. They coexist with imines, thiones, dense halogen substitution and sometimes cumulated unsaturation.
The 117-heavy-atom witness contains numerous ring junctions, halogens and heteroatom-rich linkages. Its connectivity and size make a practical synthesis difficult to assess from a graph alone.
There are 55 small all-aromatic-ring flags and 656 molecules with unassigned stereocentres. These are structural-review needs, not measured instability or an automatic invalidity verdict.
missing_features: A reliable supply of compact, differentiated heteroaromatic ring/linker arrangements at the observed Parent score level is missing from this Child panel; the exact useful arrangement cannot be specified from scores alone.

Stable attachment chemistry is underrepresented among leading decorated frameworks: 55 of the pooled highest 87 contain O-O bonds and 61 contain N-halogen bonds. More ring content is not the missing ingredient.
Configurations for the many newly formed stereogenic ring junctions and substituent centres are unspecified; no configuration-sensitive score benefit is established.

liabilities: N-halogen and O-halogen bonds occur in 74 and 71 products. The high-score cohort has fewer of the defined alerts, but this does not isolate a chemical cause of score changes.
Unassigned stereocentres, bridged ring geometries and flexible polyamine chains leave the three-dimensional structure and synthetic route unresolved.
Very large multicarbonyl/sulfonyl/polyamine assemblies and tiny halogenated fragments coexist with otherwise plausible medium-sized leaders.
missing_features: The generator already produces amines and rings; the missing capability is reliably preserving their useful spatially constrained connectivity while changing other positions. Low-score witnesses can retain nitrogen but lose the higher-score aromatic framework.

Defined configurations and an explicit exploration of relevant ionization states are not represented in this task: 850/870 products have unassigned stereocentres and all recorded graphs are formally neutral. The trajectories do not prove that adding charge or assigning stereo improves the score.

Additional ring amines are not justified as a blanket prescription: 342 products already match the ring nonamide-amine proxy. A particular basic heterocycle cannot be declared absent or required from these observations.

Dense fused/bridged architectures, aminal-like connectivities and unspecified ring-junction stereochemistry make synthetic plausibility questionable even when no simple alert matches.

missing_features: A consistent supply of compact, well-organized ring/linker geometries retaining the carbonyl and nitrogen functionality is not demonstrated at the Parent upper score level. This is a connectivity limitation, not an absence of nitrogen or ring systems.

Numerous skeleton edits do not establish useful new chemistry: equal-score N/S variants and the lower-scoring oversized concatenation show that structural novelty alone does not identify a missing feature.

Defined stereochemical relationships in the partly saturated and bridged ring systems are missing; 803/870 products have unassigned centres and no score sensitivity to their configuration has been measured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The two first cited seed-2 products score exactly 0.22131333406899525 despite replacing a nitrogen linkage by sulfur within the same overall ring framework. They retain an ethoxy/propyl aryl group and a carbonyl-bearing N-methyl ring system. Seed-0 and seed-1 leaders score 0.22016061284686828 and 0.20635925798906957 on other multiring frameworks. C#C and ClOSCl score 0.0. The 65-heavy-atom, twelve-ring concatenation scores only 0.12067644628638328. The Parent seed-2 best is a more compact 31-heavy-atom, five-ring aromatic/N-carbonyl structure at 0.24240057874100313. The observations support retaining organized N-carbonyl and aromatic/partly saturated ring connectivity, not simply adding aromatic atoms, rings or molecular mass. The pooled highest 87 Child products still occupy 39 generic scaffolds; many topological variants remain in the upper band.

per_task.generated_character: The main family is a fused N-rich bicyclic carbonyl/imino or carbonyl/thione core carrying fluorinated unsaturated or partly saturated ring substituents. The seed-0 leader includes a four-membered imine-containing ring and a seven-membered N-containing unsaturated ring, with multiple N-F and C-F bonds. Seed-1 has a thione-containing core with imine-rich substituent rings; seed-2 includes an N-chloro aziridine and an aryl aminofluoromethyl group. N-fluorinated unsaturated rings, N-chloro aziridine and small imine-containing rings require stability, strain and synthetic-route scrutiny; numerical objective values do not answer those questions.
Late small-fragment emissions discard the connected heterocyclic framework, while rare oversized concatenations are also extremely low scoring.
missing_features: A broader range of moderately sized, plausibly connected fluorinated heterocycles is missing from the high-score cohort, which repeatedly returns to a few N-carbonyl/imino cores.

Reliable retention of ordinary non-halogenated amine functionality while varying ring connectivity is not demonstrated here: the ring nonamide-amine proxy occurs in 30/870 Child products versus 250/870 Parent products. This difference is descriptive and does not prove the source of the score gap.
Specified configurations for the fluorinated saturated centres and small-ring substituents are absent; 740/870 products have unassigned centres. Their value to the score is unknown.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-0 pair in the first two citations both score 0.6843594080755538 at evaluations 211 and 222 despite moving the fluorinated ring nitrogen. Both have 30 heavy atoms. The seed-1 and seed-2 leaders score 0.5899496476575751 and 0.5094222288169709. The 51-heavy-atom, highly elaborated imino/carbonyl aromatic assembly scores 1.5347023062636605e-41, while the 57-heavy-atom carbonyl-rich concatenation scores 5.853627437068872e-35. The terminal NC1CS1 fragment scores 1.4170297216331978e-17. The visible gradient favors a moderate size and a specific fluorinated heterocyclic composition, not arbitrary size reduction or heteroatom accumulation. The Parent leaders are compact related N-heterocyclic frameworks; two retain ordinary ring amine connectivity, while all still carry structural concerns. The Child pooled highest 87 products occupy only five generic scaffolds, versus ten in the Parent high-score cohort. These data do not reveal a required target structure or establish a causal benefit for any particular amine or fluorination pattern.

The base-absent purchased subset alone contains 1,098, 423 and 305 such products. These are exact connectivity counts, not measured stability or a causal explanation of objective values. transferable_gaps.gap: The sampled output lacks consistent local chemical compatibility when attaching halogens and heteroatoms to an otherwise useful framework.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to distinguish ordinary carbon substitution from chemically distinct N-halogen, O-halogen and peroxide formation, and test whether context-sensitive attachment choices preserve useful ring and functional-group connectivity. Any future restriction is a new intervention, not a benefit established by these descriptive flags.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to create, preserve and vary chemically meaningful stereochemical assignments during graph edits, including ring-junction and substituted saturated centres. The graph flags are review cues; neither their presence nor their absence alone establishes synthetic accessibility or justifies a promised score gain.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic edit system would need to distinguish amine, amide, imine, aromatic and heteroatom-halogen nitrogen environments, and allow useful functionality to survive scaffold changes without prescribing a particular ring or receptor-specific motif. The observed associations identify a capability to test, not chemical mediation or an established component contribution.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
